derivations.claim: Given $\varepsilon>0$, use [L1] to choose a polynomial $p$ with $\|f-p\|_\infty<\varepsilon/(2(b-a))$.
The product $(f-p)\sin(nt)$ is continuous and integrable by [L5]; [L2] with its pointwise bounds gives absolute integral less than $\varepsilon/2$.
For positive $n$, apply [L3] with $u=p$ and $v=-\cos(nt)/n$, using [L4]. Bound the boundary terms and $\int p'\cos(nt)$ by [L2] to get $|\int_a^b p(t)\sin(nt)dt|\le C_p/n$.
Choose a positive integer $N$ with $C_p/N<\varepsilon/2$; then step 2.1 is below $\varepsilon/2$ for every $n\ge N$.
Split the integral into the $(f-p)$ and $p$ parts and combine steps 1.2 and 2.2 to obtain the sine limit.
Repeat steps 1.2–3.1 with $v=\sin(nt)/n$ and [L4] to obtain the cosine version.
